groups.label: Find
groups.description: Can AI search tools and assistants reach the shop and find their way round it?

groups.label: Read
groups.description: Is the content quick to read without a browser: a short llms.txt, real text in the HTML, honest error pages?

groups.label: Understand
groups.description: Does the shop describe itself in a form machines can parse: metadata and structured data?

groups.label: Trust
groups.description: Can an AI agent confirm the business is real, and does the shop let agents in?

checks.title: Home page loads
checks.description: Every AI tool starts at the home page. If it doesn't load for them, nothing else is read.
checks.fix: Make sure the store view's secure base URL answers 200 with HTML. On a dev or staging site, basic authentication or a maintenance page will fail this check.

checks.title: robots.txt
checks.description: Crawlers read robots.txt before anything else. If it errors, they treat the whole site as off limits; it is also where they find the sitemap.
checks.fix: In Magento, edit it under Content > Design > Configuration > (store view) > Search Engine Robots. Serve it as text/plain and add a line such as "Sitemap: https://www.example.com/sitemap.xml".

checks.title: AI search crawlers allowed
checks.description: These crawlers build the indexes that ChatGPT search, Claude and Perplexity answer from. If robots.txt blocks them, the shop can't be found or cited in AI search.
checks.fix: In robots.txt, don't disallow "/" for these crawlers (or for "*" without allowing them by name). Keep the checkout, customer account and search result pages disallowed. A dev or staging site should keep blocking everything.

checks.title: AI assistants allowed
checks.description: These agents fetch a page when a person asks an assistant about it, for example to compare products. Blocking them stops the assistant from answering about the shop.
checks.fix: Allow these user agents in robots.txt for the public pages, as for the AI search crawlers.

checks.title: AI training crawlers
checks.description: These collect content to train AI models. Whether to allow them is the shop's choice and doesn't affect the score.
checks.fix: No action needed. To opt out of training, disallow these user agents in robots.txt; search and assistant access is unaffected.

checks.title: XML sitemap
checks.description: A sitemap lists every page worth reading, with when it last changed.
checks.fix: In Magento, generate one under Marketing > SEO & Search > Site Map, schedule it under Stores > Configuration > Catalog > XML Sitemap, and name it in robots.txt with a Sitemap: line.

checks.title: llms.txt published
checks.description: llms.txt is a short Markdown guide to the site written for AI tools: what the business is, with links to its key pages.
checks.fix: Switch it on under Stores > Configuration > SOZO Design > llms.txt > General, fill in the Introduction, and press Generate llms.txt now.

checks.title: llms.txt is a short index
checks.description: llms.txt should be a navigation index of at most about 30,000 characters. AI agents stop reading at about 100,000, so anything after that is never seen.
checks.fix: The module keeps llms.txt under 30,000 characters and puts the rest in /llms-full.txt. If this still fails, shorten Details and When to Use This Site, or lower Category Levels.

checks.title: llms.txt links work
checks.description: A link that doesn't load wastes an agent's time and makes the file look unreliable.
checks.fix: Regenerate llms.txt after changing URLs. Check the failing pages are enabled for this store view and not behind a login.

checks.title: Guidance on when to use the shop
checks.description: Agents choose sources by fit. A short, specific "when to use this site" section tells them which questions the shop is the right answer for.
checks.fix: Fill in When to Use This Site under Stores > Configuration > SOZO Design > llms.txt > Introduction, for example: "Use this shop when someone wants to buy, compare or get advice on ...". Then generate llms.txt again.

checks.title: Content without JavaScript
checks.description: Most AI crawlers don't run JavaScript. The home page's main text and one clear <h1> heading must be in the HTML itself.
checks.fix: Make sure the home page content is in a CMS page or block rendered on the server, not loaded by JavaScript (for example from a page builder widget or slider only), and that the theme outputs one <h1>.

checks.title: Missing pages return 404
checks.description: If a missing page answers 200, an agent can't tell an error page from real content.
checks.fix: Magento answers 404 by default. If this fails, check custom routers or redirect modules that send unknown URLs to the home page with a 200.

checks.title: Page metadata
checks.description: A canonical link, the page language, a meta description and Open Graph tags tell agents which URL to cite, in which language, and how to show it.
checks.fix: Turn on canonical links under Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Catalog > Search Engine Optimization, set the home page's Meta Description on its CMS page, and make sure the theme outputs <html lang> and Open Graph tags (og:image, og:type).

checks.title: Structured data (JSON-LD)
checks.description: JSON-LD lets an agent read who the business is without guessing from the page layout.
checks.fix: Add schema.org Organization (or Store / OnlineStore) JSON-LD to the home page, with name, url and logo. Many SEO modules can output it; check it with the Schema.org validator.

checks.title: Business contact details
checks.description: Contact details, an address and links to the business's profiles (sameAs) let an agent confirm it is real and tell it apart from businesses with similar names.
checks.fix: Add contactPoint (or telephone and email), address (a PostalAddress) and sameAs (links to social profiles and listings) to the Organization JSON-LD.

checks.title: About, contact and privacy pages
checks.description: Agents look for these pages before recommending a business. Each should be linked from the home page and have real content.
checks.fix: Link the About, Contact and Privacy pages from the footer, and give each at least a few paragraphs. Make sure they are listed in llms.txt.

checks.title: AI agents not blocked

user_agents.name: ChatGPT-User
user_agents.value: Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko); compatible; ChatGPT-User/1.0; +https://openai.com/bot

user_agents.name: Claude-User
user_agents.value: Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko; compatible; Claude-User/1.0; +Claude-User@anthropic.com)

user_agents.name: PerplexityBot
user_agents.value: Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko; compatible; PerplexityBot/1.0; +https://perplexity.ai/perplexitybot)

checks.description: A firewall or bot rule that blocks AI agents stops them even when robots.txt allows them. This asks for the home page with each agent's User-Agent, from this server.
checks.fix: In Cloudflare (or the server firewall), allow verified AI search and assistant bots rather than blocking by User-Agent. This test comes from the shop's own server, so a firewall that checks the bots' real IP addresses may treat the real agents differently.
